content.overview: Section 179 provides that the Board of Directors of a company shall be entitled to exercise all such powers, and to do all such acts and things, as the company is authorised to exercise and do, except those powers which the Act, the memorandum or the articles require to be exercised or done by the company in general meeting. Certain powers listed in sub-section (3) — including making calls, authorising buy-back, issuing securities, borrowing moneys, investing funds, granting loans or giving guarantees, approving financial statements and the Board’s report, diversifying business, approving amalgamations, and taking over or acquiring a controlling interest — may be exercised only by means of resolutions passed at meetings of the Board. The Board may, by a resolution passed at a meeting, delegate certain of those powers to a committee, managing director, manager or other principal officer on such conditions as it may specify.
content.glance: Board exercises all company powers except those reserved to the general meeting; listed powers in s. 179(3) only by Board meeting resolution; limited delegation permitted.
content.study: The Board of Directors of a company shall be entitled to exercise all such powers, and to do all such acts and things, as the company is authorised to exercise and do: Provided that in exercising such power or doing such act or thing, the Board shall be subject to the provisions contained in that behalf in this Act, or in the memorandum or articles, or in any regulations not inconsistent therewith and duly made thereunder, including regulations made by the company in general meeting. No regulation made by the company in general meeting shall invalidate any prior act of the Board which would have been valid if that regulation had not been made. The Board may exercise certain powers only by resolutions passed at meetings of the Board, including making calls on shareholders, authorising buy-back under section 68, issuing securities including debentures, borrowing moneys, investing the funds of the company, granting loans or giving guarantee or providing security, approving financial statement and the Board’s report, diversifying the business, approving amalgamation, merger or reconstruction, and taking over a company or acquiring a controlling or substantial stake. The Board may, by a resolution passed at a meeting, delegate to any committee of directors, the managing director, the manager or any other principal officer of the company, any of the powers specified in clauses (d) to (f) of sub-section (3) on such conditions as it may specify. Current-law framing: identify the power; check whether it is reserved to the general meeting (s. 180 and MOA/AOA); if it is a s. 179(3) power, require a Board meeting resolution; test any delegation.

sections.heading: General Power
sections.body: Board may exercise all powers the company is authorised to exercise, subject to the Act, memorandum, articles and valid regulations, except powers reserved to the general meeting.

sections.heading: Meeting-Only Powers (s. 179(3))
sections.body: Calls, buy-back, issue of securities, borrowing, investing funds, loans/guarantees/security, approval of financial statements and Board’s report, diversification, amalgamation/merger/reconstruction, and taking over or acquiring controlling interest — only by resolution at a Board meeting.

sections.heading: Delegation
sections.body: Board may by meeting resolution delegate specified powers (borrowing, investing, loans/guarantees) to a committee, MD, manager or principal officer on stated conditions.

examples.title: Borrowing by circulation
examples.body: The Board attempts to authorise substantial borrowing solely by circular resolution. Section 179(3) requires a resolution passed at a Board meeting for borrowing moneys.

examples.title: Delegation of investment power
examples.body: The Board by meeting resolution delegates the power to invest funds to a committee on stated conditions. That is permitted under s. 179 for the specified powers.

hypotheticals.question: Can the general meeting take away a power already validly exercised by the Board?
hypotheticals.analysis: A regulation made by the company in general meeting does not invalidate any prior act of the Board which would have been valid if that regulation had not been made. Prospective reservation is different from invalidating past valid Board acts.

distinctions.title: Powers of Board (s. 179) vs restrictions requiring special resolution (s. 180)
distinctions.left: Board’s residual and listed powers, some only at meetings
distinctions.right: Specified high-impact acts need members’ special resolution

misconceptions.trap: All Board powers can be exercised by circular resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Powers listed in s. 179(3) must be exercised by resolutions passed at meetings of the Board, not by circulation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 179 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the power. II. Check reservation to general meeting. III. If s. 179(3), require Board meeting resolution. IV. Test delegation. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Power facts; meeting vs circulation; reservation; delegation; precise relief.

examTips: Board residual power subject to Act/MOA/AOA.
